brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Color-coded topic clusters create immediate categorical legibility — each group has its own distinct accent hue with consistent saturation
Spatial clustering with labeled topic regions communicates the 'proximity = relatedness' concept clearly at first glance
Card treatment with colored top-edge accent and dark body feels crafted and gives a tactile, sticker-like quality
dominant_weaknesses: Card titles truncate aggressively ('Componen', 'Configurati', 'Documenta') — text sizing ignores actual content length, breaking scanability
Cluster placement looks arbitrary rather than meaningful; distance between clusters carries no visible semantic weight or hierarchy
Cards within clusters overlap and stagger inconsistently, suggesting messiness rather than intentional spatial relationships
fix_priorities: Fix text truncation: widen cards or wrap to two lines so every title is fully readable
Establish a spatial logic — proximity rules, gravitational pull, or axis meaning — so position carries information
Add visual connectors or soft territory shapes around clusters to reinforce grouping over the current floating-cards feel
Introduce a minimap/zoom affordance (the bottom-right box hints at this) with clearer state and interaction cues
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral appeal from color clusters is strong, but behavioral clarity suffers from truncation and unclear spatial semantics, leaving reflective novelty to carry the concept.
rationale.intent_fit: It gestures at spatial-canvas organization through clustered colored cards, but the layout still reads as loosely-arranged groups rather than a meaningful proximity-driven map.
